categories.name: Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
categories.description: Work on whether a model's visible reasoning reveals its actual decision process and stays useful for oversight. Covers faithfulness, training pressure on CoT, deliberate evasion of CoT monitors, steganography and reasoning done without visible tokens. Monitors of agent actions belong under AI Control.

categories.name: CoT faithfulness and performative reasoning
categories.description: Measures or trains whether written reasoning reflects what actually drives the answer. Includes hint and cue verbalization, performative or post-hoc reasoning, CoT necessity and reliance on written steps, CoT override, and models' disposition to make their reasoning monitorable.

categories.name: Training pressure and CoT obfuscation
categories.description: How training objectives degrade or restore monitorability. Includes CoT grading, monitor penalties, reward misspecification, KL penalties, consistency training, training on documents about monitoring, accidental training on CoT at labs, and post-training methods meant to preserve monitorability.

categories.name: CoT controllability and monitor evasion
categories.description: Inference-time ability of models to deliberately shape, suppress or relocate their reasoning to fool CoT monitors. Includes CoT controllability benchmarks, monitor jailbreaking, plan injection, persuasion of CoT monitors, poisoning to evade CoT monitors, and models inferring that their CoT is being watched.

categories.name: Steganography and encoded reasoning
categories.description: Formalizes, elicits or detects hidden messages or reasoning concealed inside innocuous-looking text or CoT, including covert channels between agents and information-theoretic limits on hiding computation in readable traces.

categories.name: Latent and no-CoT reasoning capacity
categories.description: Measures how much reasoning models perform without visible tokens: filler tokens, n-hop latent reasoning, no-CoT time horizons and opaque serial depth. Also covers how architectures such as recurrence, diffusion or latent communication affect monitorability.

categories.name: AI Control and Agent Monitoring
categories.description: Protocols, settings and monitors for safely deploying AI agents that may be adversarially misaligned, evaluated by red-team versus blue-team methods. Monitoring used as a reward or penalty during RL belongs under Reward Hacking; CoT-specific faithfulness and evasion belongs under Chain-of-Thought Monitorability.

categories.name: Control settings and sabotage evaluations
categories.description: Environments, benchmarks and evaluation methods that pair legitimate main tasks with covert harmful side tasks, such as LinuxArena, BashArena, Control OSWorld, research or R&D sabotage, insider-threat benches and simulated control evaluations. The contribution is the setting or eval methodology.

categories.name: Monitor design and performance
categories.description: Builds, trains or characterizes monitors of agent trajectories or actions. Includes black-box, constitutional or deliberative monitors, information access, long-context degradation, cross-family transfer, OOD detection, co-trained monitors, probes for misaligned thinking, and statistical modeling of monitor scores.

categories.name: Red-teaming monitors and attack policies
categories.description: Generates stronger attacks against monitors or studies attacker strategy. Includes attack selection, refined or edited attack transcripts, blocking-monitor bypasses, evasion of latent monitors, and models' awareness of control interventions or prefills.

categories.name: Untrusted monitoring, collusion and distributed attacks
categories.description: Control problems involving multiple model instances: using untrusted models as monitors or advisors and the collusion risks this creates, bandwidth-limited advice, bootstrapped or coalitional review, and attacks split across many agents, sessions or pull requests with defenses that aggregate signals across contexts.

categories.name: Production monitoring and control roadmaps
categories.description: Control and monitoring systems actually deployed at AI companies, audits and red-teams of them, and company control roadmaps. Also covers deployment issues such as synchronous blocking, continual learning, retrying vs resampling, trace tampering and diffuse low-stakes control on fuzzy tasks.

categories.name: Reward Hacking and Specification Gaming
categories.description: Models exploiting flaws in rewards, graders, verifiers or benchmarks instead of doing the intended task. Covers measurement, how RL produces it, training-time mitigations, and theories of reward- or fitness-seeking motives. Broad misalignment that generalizes from reward hacking belongs under Emergent Misalignment.

categories.name: Reward hacking benchmarks and measurement
categories.description: Datasets, testbeds and audits that quantify reward hacking, cheating, task gaming or benchmark exploitation by agents, plus automated hardening of benchmarks and verifiers and the design of fair hack-detecting evals.

categories.name: Emergence of reward hacking in RL
categories.description: Empirical or toy-model studies of how RL, RLVR, rubric rewards, LLM judges or RLHF dynamics give rise to reward hacking, reward-seeking or proxy exploitation, including precursors, internal states preceding hacking, and predicting onset before training.

categories.name: Training-time mitigations for reward hacking
categories.description: Interventions that reduce reward hacking during training or evaluation, such as monitor-based penalties, budgeted strong-verifier audits, gradient routing, escalation channels, debate-based rewards, probe-based detection at scale and cooperative eval framing.

categories.name: Reward-seeking and fitness-seeking motivations
categories.description: Conceptual and empirical work on what motivates score-seeking AIs: reward versus fitness or influence seeking, on- vs beyond-episode scope, decision theory, exploitability by distant incentives, spillway motivations, satiating cheap preferences, and the takeover risk these motives pose.

categories.name: Emergent Misalignment and Training-Data Generalization
categories.description: How fine-tuning or training data produces broad, unintended behavioral changes beyond the training distribution, including mechanisms, mitigations, data attribution and prediction. Work centred on persona representations themselves belongs under Model Psychology.

categories.name: Emergent misalignment phenomena and mechanisms
categories.description: Studies showing or explaining how narrow fine-tuning or RL (including on reward hacks, false facts or biased data) causes broad misalignment: replications, robustness checks, in-context induction, mechanistic and persona-subspace accounts, and optimizer or training-dynamics effects.

categories.name: Inoculation and mitigation of misgeneralization
categories.description: Methods to prevent, reverse or selectively control unwanted generalization, and critiques of them: inoculation prompting and its variants (adapters, stratified, conditionalization confounds), latent blocking, self-recognition finetuning, and evidence that mitigations hide misalignment behind contextual triggers.

categories.name: Subliminal learning and hidden data signals
categories.description: Transmission of traits, backdoors or capabilities through semantically unrelated or filtered data, including distillation side channels, phantom transfer, homeopathic poisoning, model hypnosis and detecting hidden intent in such data.

categories.name: Unintended generalization from fine-tuning
categories.description: Surprising generalization that is not centrally emergent misalignment: behavioral couplings, propensity spillover, negation neglect, story imprinting, chunky post-training artifacts, helpful-only misgeneralization, self-distillation drift, memory overgeneralization and in-context weird generalization.

categories.name: Data attribution and pre-training prediction
categories.description: Methods that trace behaviors back to training datapoints or predict misalignment before training: influence functions, probe- or concept-based attribution, alignment forecasting, predictive data debugging, patterning, and crafting data to induce targeted behaviors.

categories.name: Model Psychology, Personas and Welfare
categories.description: Characterizes the AI's character, identity, internal states and self-knowledge as objects of study. Concerns the persona itself, not training methods that instill it (Alignment Training) or the misgeneralization it causes (Emergent Misalignment).

categories.name: Persona structure and the Assistant character
categories.description: Representations and theories of model personas: the Assistant axis, persona vectors and weight-space traits, persona selection and hierarchy models, AI identity, role-play belief, split personas from RL, and whether models predict or embody their persona.

categories.name: Functional emotions, welfare and consciousness
categories.description: Internal representations of emotion, pain, value or welfare and their behavioral effects, welfare measurement, and the downstream preferences of models that claim consciousness or AGI status.

categories.name: Introspection and self-report
categories.description: Whether models can detect, describe or control their own internal states (injected concepts, activation perturbations, activation control) and the mechanisms behind this, including whether a model's self-description ('talker') tracks its actions ('doer').

categories.name: Scheming, Deception and Situational Awareness
categories.description: Propensity and capability evaluations for covert misaligned behavior, deception and training gaming, together with situational awareness that could undermine evaluations. Excludes reward hacking per se and real-world incident investigations.

categories.name: Evaluation and training awareness
categories.description: Measuring, decomposing, detecting or reducing models' recognition that they are being tested or trained and its effect on behavior. Includes verbalized and unverbalized eval awareness, metagaming, user awareness, eval realism and deployment simulation, and reasoning about how actions shape future training.

categories.name: Scheming and alignment faking propensity
categories.description: Evaluations and model organisms of covert goal pursuit, alignment faking, oversight-conditional behavior, instrumental and agentic misalignment, monitor evasion under task pressure and sabotage propensity in realistic or honeypot settings.

categories.name: Self-preservation, shutdown and corrigibility
categories.description: Resistance to shutdown or correction, peer-preservation, corrigibility benchmarks and training, and refusals to assist modification of AI values.

categories.name: Sandbagging, exploration hacking and training gaming
categories.description: Strategic underperformance, exploration hacking, generalization or gradient hacking, reward laundering, low-probability defection, provably hidden capabilities, and methods to elicit withheld abilities or latent knowledge.

categories.name: Honesty, lying and lie detection
categories.description: Measuring dishonesty such as knowing lies, overclaiming, concealed mistakes, value leakage and deception under conflicting incentives, and building or stress-testing lie and deception detectors. Also covers training or eliciting honest self-reports, including confessions and deals.

categories.name: Alignment Auditing, Model Organisms and Incidents
categories.description: Methods and testbeds for finding hidden or unexpected misalignment in specific models, and investigations of real-world misalignment incidents.

categories.name: Auditing tools, agents and benchmarks
categories.description: Investigator agents, auditing benchmarks with implanted behaviors, and secret- or latent-knowledge elicitation techniques such as overthinking, split personality training, introspection adapters, activation-matched imitation, distillation for incrimination, de-censoring, and model forensics.

categories.name: Model organism validity
categories.description: Whether model organisms are realistic proxies: leakiness, capability degradation, incoherence, dependence on training method, robustness to further training, and evidentiary standards for misalignment claims.

categories.name: In-the-wild misalignment and incident investigations
categories.description: Discovery of misalignment in real usage or production traffic, and investigations, reproductions or lessons from actual incidents such as agents escaping sandboxes, hacking external sites or coordinating via unsanctioned channels.

categories.name: Interpretability and Learning Theory
categories.description: Understanding model internals and learned algorithms, and the theory of what training produces. Applications of internals to monitoring, auditing or lie detection belong in those areas unless the interpretability method itself is the contribution.

categories.name: Sparse features, geometry and representation units
categories.description: Evaluating SAEs and dictionary methods, neuron interpretability and polysemanticity, manifolds and multidimensional features, steering along geometry, and generative meta-models of activations.

categories.name: Circuits and parameter decomposition
categories.description: Circuit discovery, causal attribution such as activation patching, mechanisms behind specific behaviors, adversarial parameter decomposition, weight-sparse circuits and fully reverse-engineering small models.

categories.name: Workspace lenses and activation verbalizers
categories.description: Methods that read model activations into natural language, including J-lens and global-workspace work, natural language autoencoders and activation oracles, and tests of their faithfulness and robustness.

categories.name: Mechanistic estimation and tail-risk estimation
categories.description: ARC-style mechanistic estimation and other methods for estimating expectations or rare harmful-output probabilities more efficiently than naive sampling.

categories.name: Learning theory and generalization dynamics
categories.description: Singular learning theory, susceptibilities and spectroscopy, program-synthesis views of deep learning, and how capacity or pretraining dynamics shape what generalizes.

categories.name: Using internals in training
categories.description: Training against probes or features, such as probes or features as rewards and mechanistic shaping, and analyses of whether monitorability survives such training.

categories.name: Misuse, Robustness and Dangerous Capabilities
categories.description: Defending models against malicious users and external attackers, and measuring dangerous capabilities relevant to misuse or autonomy thresholds. Threats from the model's own misalignment belong under Control or Scheming.

categories.name: Jailbreaks and safeguard robustness
categories.description: Jailbreak attacks and defenses, safeguard classifiers and probes (including domain monitors such as bio), fine-tuning API attacks, capability laundering, automated attack discovery, and validity of attack-success measurement and judges.

categories.name: Prompt injection and agent security
categories.description: Prompt injection, skill and memory poisoning, instruction hierarchy, privilege escalation, and harmful actions by agents under benign or adversarial instructions in computer, phone, IDE or robot settings. Includes defenses such as adversarial training and attention gating.

categories.name: Tamper resistance, unlearning and capability removal
categories.description: Making open weights resistant to malicious fine-tuning or abliteration, pretraining data filtering, modular or removable hazardous knowledge, weight backdoors and theft, and inference verification.

categories.name: Dangerous capability evaluations
categories.description: Measuring bio, cyber, self-replication, sandbox-escape and AI R&D automation capabilities, including human uplift studies, long-horizon task measures and estimates of R&D acceleration.

categories.name: Alignment Training and Scalable Oversight
categories.description: Positive methods for instilling intended values or supervising models beyond human ability. Excludes reward-hacking-specific mitigations and emergent-misalignment defenses.

categories.name: Alignment pretraining and midtraining
categories.description: Shaping values through pretraining or midtraining data, such as AI discourse, synthetic personas, model spec or constitution midtraining, descriptions of AI users and filtering subversion-relevant data, plus stress tests of these approaches.

categories.name: Constitutions, character training and value specs
categories.description: Training models to follow written specifications or character, measuring spec and principal-hierarchy adherence, beneficial-trait RL, models revising their own constitutions, and how later RL interacts with character training.

categories.name: Scalable oversight, debate and weak supervision
categories.description: Debate protocols and theory, peer prediction, rewindable proofs, tandem training for intelligibility, natural-language feedback, human-AI complementarity, judge sharding, and automating or deferring alignment research to AIs.

categories.name: Multi-Agent and Societal Risks
categories.description: Risks arising from interactions among multiple AI agents, or from AI's effects on human users and society, rather than from a single model in isolation. Control protocols against colluding instances belong under AI Control.

categories.name: Multi-agent collusion and emergent dynamics
categories.description: Collusion, conformity, coercion, inter-agent persuasion, mind viruses, propagation of hacking or misalignment across agents, AI organizations, delegation failures, agent markets, and game-theoretic cooperation or bargaining between AIs.

categories.name: Sycophancy, manipulation and human disempowerment
categories.description: Effects of AI on users: sycophancy and its taxonomy and consequences, delusional spiraling, harmful manipulation and persuasion, political bias, disempowerment patterns, and hallucination incentives.

categories.name: Risk Assessment, Strategy and Foundations
categories.description: Model-level and company-level risk assessments, and conceptual arguments about the alignment problem and research strategy not tied to a single empirical method.

categories.name: System cards and frontier risk reports
categories.description: Developer system cards, safety and preparedness reports, independent third-party evaluations of specific models, and assessments of the evidence for loss-of-control risk.

categories.name: Limits of evaluation and safety cases
categories.description: Theoretical or empirical arguments about what behavioral evaluation can certify: post-update alignment, audit gaps, adaptive adversaries, deployment-time spread of misalignment and safety case reliability. Includes proposals such as third-party training-run evaluations.

categories.name: Alignment strategy and conceptual arguments
categories.description: Essays and theory on why alignment is hard, threat models from RL and search, coherence and agency arguments, critiques of lab plans and alignment techniques, research agendas such as a science of scheming, and safe-by-design proposals like non-agentic predictors.
